approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would create new accountability rules for banks, insurers and superannuation funds, and its schedules make changes to other laws to support that framework.

The main mechanism is the Financial Accountability Regime Bill 2022, which would force these industries to meet higher responsibility standards, with this bill making the necessary consequential amendments.
The new rules would apply to banks six months after the main bill starts, and to insurers and superannuation providers 18 months after its commencement.
Consequential amendments would be made to relevant Acts to support the accountability regime.
The bill's schedules would commence at the same time as the Financial Accountability Regime Bill 2022.
Amendments under this bill would take effect when the regime applies to the banking industry, six months after the main bill starts.
The banking, insurance and superannuation industries and their new entrants would be affected.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2022-12-01.395.2) introduced by ACT Senator [Katy Gallagher](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/act/katy_gallagher) (Labor), which means it passed. ### Motion text > *That—* > > *(a) after consideration of the [Animal Health Australia and Plant Health Australia Funding Legislation Amendment Bill 2022](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r6913) has concluded, the questions on all remaining stages of the [Financial Sector Reform Bill 2022](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r6909) only be put without debate; and* > > *(b) paragraph (a) operate as a limitation of debate under [standing order 142](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Chamber_documents/Senate_chamber_documents/standingorders/b00/b20#standing-order_c20-142).*

The Financial Sector Reform Bill 2022 implements remaining banking royal commission recommendations, including a Compensation Scheme of Last Resort (CSLR) providing up to $150,000 for unpaid Australian Financial Complaints Authority determinations, and strengthens consumer protections for small amount credit contracts and consumer leases with new caps, repayment rules, and prohibitions.
